{{Short description|Complex simple Lie Algebra}}
In mathematics, an '''exceptional Lie algebra''' is a complex [[simple Lie algebra]] whose [[Dynkin diagram]] is of exceptional (nonclassical) type.<ref>{{harvnb|Fulton|Harris|1991|loc=Theorem 9.26.}}</ref> There are exactly five of them: <math>\mathfrak{g}_2, \mathfrak{f}_4, \mathfrak{e}_6, \mathfrak{e}_7, \mathfrak{e}_8</math>; their respective dimensions are 14, 52, 78, 133, 248.<ref name=Knapp>{{harvnb|Knapp|2002|loc=Appendix C, § 2.}}</ref> The corresponding diagrams are:<ref>{{harvnb|Fulton|Harris|1991|loc=§ 21.2.}}</ref>
*[[G2 (mathematics)|G<sub>2</sub>]]: {{Dynkin2|node|6a|node}}
*[[F4 (mathematics)|F<sub>4</sub>]]: {{Dynkin2|node|3|node|4a|node|3|node}}
*[[E6 (mathematics)|E<sub>6</sub>]]: {{Dynkin2|node|3|node|3|branch|3|node|3|node}}
*[[E7 (mathematics)|E<sub>7</sub>]]: {{Dynkin2|node|3|node|3|branch|3|node|3|node|3|node}}
*[[E8 (mathematics)|E<sub>8</sub>]]: {{Dynkin2|node|3|node|3|branch|3|node|3|node|3|node|3|node}}

In contrast, simple Lie algebras that are not exceptional are called [[classical Lie algebra]]s (there are infinitely many of them).

== Construction ==
There is no simple universally accepted way to construct exceptional Lie algebras; in fact, they were discovered only in the process of the classification program. Here are some constructions:
*§ 22.1-2 from Fulton and Harris' book<ref>{{Cite book |last=Fulton |first=William |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4612-0979-9 |title=Representation Theory |last2=Harris |first2=Joe |date=2004 |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-3-540-00539-1 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=129 |location=New York, NY |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-0979-9}}</ref> give a detailed construction of <math>\mathfrak{g}_2</math>.
*Exceptional Lie algebras may be realized as the derivation algebras of appropriate nonassociative algebras.
*Construct <math>\mathfrak{e}_8</math> first and then find <math>\mathfrak{e}_6, \mathfrak{e}_7</math> as subalgebras.
*[[Jacques Tits|Tits]] has given a uniformed construction of the five exceptional Lie algebras.<ref name="tits66">{{cite journal |last1=Tits |first1=Jacques |title=Algèbres alternatives, algèbres de Jordan et algèbres de Lie exceptionnelles. I. Construction |journal=Indag. Math. |date=1966 |volume=28 |pages=223–237 |doi=10.1016/S1385-7258(66)50028-2 |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82411299.pdf |access-date=9 August 2023}}</ref>
